# Adjudication Task — Chapter 510

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃510화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|선화아(船火兒) 무송은 태생부터 뱃사람이었다.
  6|
  7|얼굴도 기억나지 않는 그의 부모는 근방에 유명한 잉꼬부부 수적이었고, 외가와 친가의 가계에도 수적이나 어부가 수두룩했다.
  8|
  9|그야말로 뼈대 깊은 수적 집안.
 10|
 11|그 때문인지는 몰라도 무송은 육지보다 배에 있는 시간이 훨씬 좋았다.
 12|
 13|빽빽한 숲과 들판을 보면 극독을 먹은 것처럼 손발이 저리고 숨이 막히는데, 탁 트인 강과 바다만 보면 생기가 도는 것이다.
 14|
 15|그뿐인가. 수적 질로 한몫 단단히 잡은 다른 채주들이 그럴듯한 장원을 매입하고 기루에서 주색잡기를 즐길 때, 그는 배를 꾸미고 그물을 엮어 만든 침대에 누워 장강을 구경했다.
 16|
 17|그리고 그럴 때마다 무송이 늘 하는 생각이 있었다.
 18|
 19|‘천하가 온통 물로 이루어졌으면 좋겠다. 그럼 평생 배에서만 지낼 수 있을 텐데.’
 20|
 21|하지만 지금, 무송은 멍하니 장강을 응시하며 중얼거리고 있었다.
 22|
 23|“아, 씨바. 배 존나 느리네. 빨리 내리고 싶다…….”
 24|
 25|“……!”
 26|
 27|“……!”
 28|
 29|순간 싸해지는 분위기.
 30|
 31|주위에 있던 수룡채의 수적들은 순간 자신들의 귀를 의심했다.
 32|
 33|그리고 눈동자를 뒤룩뒤룩 굴리며 눈짓을 주고받던 그들은 얼마 가지 않아 명쾌한 결론을 내렸다.
 34|
 35|‘우리가 잘못 들었나 보네!’
 36|
 37|‘그거 맞다. 단체로 귀가 잘못된 게 틀림없어.’
 38|
 39|‘두목께서 그런 말을 하실 리 없지.’
 40|
 41|무송이 어떤 사람인지는 수룡채의 최고참부터 막내까지, 아니 장강수로맹에 있는 수적 전부가 아는 사실이었다.
 42|
 43|뜨거운 뱃사람의 상징! 스승인 해상왕보다도 더 장강을 사랑하는 남자!
 44|
 45|그런 사람이 제 목숨만큼이나 아끼는 쾌조선을 느리다며 욕하고, 육지로 가고 싶다고 말할 리가 없…….
 46|
 47|“이 짓거리도 때려치우든가 해야지. 개 같아서 진짜.”
 48|
 49|“……!”
 50|
 51|“……!”
 52|
 53|보이지 않는 충격이 갑판을 휩쓸었다. 갑작스러운 무송의 은퇴 의사 표명과 수룡채 해체 위기에 조용해진 사방.
 54|
 55|영원히 이어질 것 같던 침묵을 깨트린 건 넋이 나간 어느 수적의 어깨에서 미끄러진 술통이었다.
 56|
 57|쿵, 콰직!
 58|
 59|술이 가득 담겨 있던지라 무게도 상당했다. 떨어진 목제 통이 박살 남과 동시에 술이 사방으로 튀었다.
 60|
 61|그제야 자신만의 상념에서 빠져나온 무송이 눈을 부라렸다.
 62|
 63|“이게 무슨 짓거리냐.”
 64|
 65|안 그래도 흉악한 면상의 소유자인 무송이다. 술통을 떨어트린 수적은 사색이 되어 넙죽 허리를 굽혔다.
 66|
 67|“죄, 죄송합니다!”
 68|
 69|“이 새끼가 술 귀한 줄 모르고 확 그냥. 거꾸로 매달아서 그 뭐냐. 장강, 장강…… 그래, 찍먹형에 처할까 보다.”
 70|
 71|“주, 죽을죄를 지었습니다. 그러니 제발 그것만은…….”
 72|
 73|“조심해라. 가뜩이나 기분 거지 같은데 초치지 말고.”
 74|
 75|“예, 옙!”
 76|
 77|“됐고, 원상복구나 시켜 놔. 술도 도로 하나 가져다 놓고.”
 78|
 79|“예? 하지만…….”
 80|
 81|“이놈이 미쳤나. 어디서 감히 토를, 어서 움직이지 못할까!”
 82|
 83|“조, 존명!”
 84|
 85|필사적인 복명복창과 함께 멀어지는 수하의 뒷모습에, 무송은 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
 86|
 87|‘뭐 하나 제대로 되는 일이 없군.’
 88|
 89|단순한 불평이 아니라, 정말 사실이 그랬다.
 90|
 91|호재만 이어져도 부족할 판국에 안 좋은 일만 잇따라 계속되고 있었다.
 92|
 93|울며 겨자 먹기로 본거지인 사천을 떠나 호북에 왔고, 얼마 전에는 친혈육 같았던 장강일도 황충을 떠나보내야 했다.
 94|
 95|그에 대한 은원(恩怨)은 갚아야 한다는 생각으로 진태경 일행을 하남까지 데려다주기로 했는데…… 아니나 다를까 최악의 상황이 벌어지고야 말았다.
 96|
 97|‘끝까지 모르는 척하려고 했는데.’
 98|
 99|반로환동 한 것이 확실해 보이는 정체불명의 노고수.
100|
101|어린 의생의 탈을 쓴 그 맹수가 자신의 정체가 탄로 났음을 알아차려 버렸다.
102|
103|‘괴물 같은 늙은이. 도대체 정체가 뭐지?’
104|
105|그간 무송이 면밀하게 관찰해 온 바에 의하면, 이 사실을 아는 사람은 함께 이동하고 있는 일행 중에서도 극소수였다. 기껏해야 화왕 적천강과 진태경 정도?
106|
107|어디로 튀는지 알 수 없는 청풍도 문경 앞에서는 조용해지는 걸 보면, 저놈도 알고 있을 확률이 높다.
108|
109|‘제기랄. 이럴 줄 알았으면 차라리 다른 배를 타는 건데.’
110|
111|현재 하남으로 향하는 수룡채의 쾌조선은 총 두 척이었다. 사람이 많으니 인원을 나눠서 타자는 건 적천강의 강요에 의해서였고, 무송에게는 감히 화왕의 뜻을 거스를 용기가 없었다.
112|
113|백여 장 앞에서 앞서가고 있는 또 다른 쾌조선에서 편안히 가고 있을 부채주를 생각하자 배가 아플 지경이다.
114|
115|‘여기에 비하면 저쪽은 꽃밭이지, 꽃밭.’
116|
117|적어도 다른 배에는 말이 통하는 인물들이 모여 있다.
118|
119|궁기방의 냄새도 잠깐만 숨을 참으면 해결될 문제고, 청풍이 미미라고 부르는 괴상한 뱀의 묘기를 보는 것도 제법 재미가 쏠쏠했다.
120|
121|반면 이쪽은?
122|
123|‘열화신룡 진태경. 화왕 적천강. 그리고 정체를 숨긴 또 다른 노괴.’
124|
125|그야말로 괴물 집합소라고 해도 과언이 아니다.
126|
127|그나마 무늬만 후배인 진태경은 무송에게 존댓말이라도 써 주고, 적천강도 자주 보다 보니 그럭저럭 사람 취급은 해 주는데 마지막 한 사람이 문제였다.
128|
129|‘그 눈빛…….’
130|
131|문경의 서늘한 눈동자를 떠올린 무송은 자신도 모르게 전신을 바르르 떨었다.
132|
133|아까부터 계속되는 두목의 이상 행동을 주목하던 고참 수적 하나가 다가와 슬쩍 물었다.
134|
135|“채주. 괜찮으십니까요?”
136|
137|“괜찮아 보이냐?”
138|
139|“전혀 아닌뎁쇼.”
140|
141|“그럼 뭘 물어봐. 어차피 사정 다 아는 놈이.”
142|
143|“거참 걱정을 해 줘도 뭐라 하시네. 그나저나 그 노괴(老怪)가 도대체 무슨 겁박을 했길래 안색이…… 읍!”
144|
145|빛의 속도로 손을 뻗어 수하의 입을 틀어막은 무송이 긴장된 눈빛으로 주위를 둘러봤다.
146|
147|들은 사람이 없다는 걸 두 번, 세 번 확인하고 나서야 비로소 분노가 솟구쳤다.
148|
149|“이런 미친놈을 봤나. 죽고 싶어서 환장했느냐?”
150|
151|“읍읍, 푸하!”
152|
153|간신히 입막음에서 벗어난 고참 수적이 말을 더듬었다.
154|
155|“죄, 죄송합니다요. 저도 모르게 그만.”
156|
157|“내 이미 여러 번 말했지만, 너와 다른 녀석들 모두 그에 관해서는 입도 벙긋하지 마라. 알겠느냐?”
158|
159|“예에.”
160|
161|고참 수적은 문경의 정체를 직접 목격한 몇 안 되는 수적 중 하나였다.
162|
163|불안하게 눈동자를 굴리는 그의 모습에 한숨을 푹 내쉰 무송이 입을 열었다.
164|
165|“그보다 아까 내가 내린 지시 사항. 모두 철저히 숙지시켜 놨느냐?”
166|
167|고참 수적이 고개를 끄덕였다.
168|
169|“그러믄입쇼. 채주께서 말씀하신 대로, 후미에는 얼씬도 하지 말라고 단단히 일러 뒀습니다요.”
170|
171|“의심하는 놈은 없었고?”
172|
173|수적들의 머릿수만 수십이다 보니, 멍청하고 눈치 없는 한두 놈은 꼭 끼어있기 마련이었다.
174|
175|“있었지요. 춘삼이. 채주의 명이라고 했는데도 세 번이나 캐묻길래 식겁했습니다요.”
176|
177|무송이 뿌드득 이를 갈았다.
178|
179|“내 그 새끼일 줄 알았지. 춘삼이 그놈 지금 어디 있느냐?”
180|
181|“장강에 푹 담갔다가 건졌는뎁쇼. 지금 아래에 처박아 뒀으니 다시는 그런 말 안 나올 겁니다요.”
182|
183|“후우, 잘했다. 앞으로 내가 자리를 비울 때도 애들 단속 철저히 해. 까딱하면 쾌조선이랑 같이 싸그리 장강에 수장(水葬)되는 수가 있다.”
184|
185|무송의 낯빛은 어두웠다.
186|
187|화왕 적천강이라는 괴물로도 부족해서, 이제는 반로환동 한 정체불명의 노괴까지 끼어 버렸다. 차라리 그 사실을 몰랐던 때가 그리워질 지경이다.
188|
189|하늘 같은 채주의 약한 모습에 고참 수적이 초조한 목소리로 물었다.
190|
191|“이러다가 두 번 다시 사천으로 못 돌아가는 거 아닙니까? 가뜩이나 벌써 두 달 가까이 수채를 비웠는데, 이대로 영영 빌까 걱정입니다요.”
192|
193|“재수 없는 소리. 호랑이 굴에 들어가도 정신만 차리면 산다고 했다.”
194|
195|“그건 호랑이고, 반로환동 한 초절정 고수한테는 정신을 골백번 차려도 안 될 것 같은디…….”
196|
197|생각해 보니 저 말이 맞다.
198|
199|말문이 막힌 무송이 조용히 입을 다문 바로 그때였다.
200|
201|“술통을 가져왔는데, 어디에 두면 되겠습니까?”
202|
203|등 뒤에서 들려오는 목소리. 이 상황에서 술통 운운할 놈은 한 사람밖에 없다.
204|
205|짜증이 솟구친 무송은 고개를 돌리기도 전에 벌컥 성을 냈다.
206|
207|“아니, 보자 보자 하니까 아까부터 저 폐급 새끼가……!”
208|
209|“지금 제게 폐급 새끼, 라고 하셨습니까.”
210|
211|“……어?”
212|
213|억겁과도 같은 촌각의 시간.
214|
215|자신의 어깨 너머를 바라보며 입을 딱 벌린 고참 수적의 모습에, 무송은 단단히 좆 됐음을 직감했다.
216|
217|더불어 잊고 있던 사실 하나가 뇌리를 스쳤다.
218|
219|‘아, 여분의 술통을 후미(後尾)에 놔뒀었구나.’
220|
221|어쩐지 다시 가져오라 할 때 뭔가 말하려다가 말더라니.
222|
223|무송은 눈앞이 아찔해졌다. 천령폭의 와류에 휘말렸을 때도 두려움을 느끼지는 않았는데, 지금은 식은땀으로 멱을 감아도 될 정도다.
224|
225|“무송 대협.”
226|
227|한차례 눈을 질끈 감은 무송이 억지웃음을 지으며 천천히 돌아섰다.
228|
229|꿈에서도 만나기 싫은 한 사람이 그곳에 있었다.
230|
231|“어, 어어. 문경이로구나. 무, 무슨 일이니?”
232|
233|“별일은 아닙니다.”
234|
235|그 나이대의 소년처럼 빙긋 웃은 문경이 대답했다.
236|
237|“후미에서 장강을 구경 중이었는데, 수하 분께서 오셨지 뭡니까. 듣기로는 무송 대협께서 술통을 가져오라 명하셨다던데…….”
238|
239|“내, 내가 말이냐?”
240|
241|“아닙니까?”
242|
243|“그, 글쎄, 나는 그런 명령을 내린 기억이…….”
244|
245|그때, 문경의 등 뒤에서 술통을 어깨에 진 수적이 나타나 빠릿빠릿하게 외쳤다.
246|
247|“채주님! 명하신 대로 술통을 가져왔습니다!”
248|
249|무송은 저놈의 주둥아리를 당장 찢어 버리고 싶은 충동을 억누르며 말을 이었다.
250|
251|“그런 명령을 내린 기억이…… 나는구나. 맞아. 그런 명령을 내리긴 했다. 명백한 실수였지.”
252|
253|“실수라. 네.”
254|
255|무송은 자신의 몸 곳곳을 차례차례 응시하는 문경의 시선을 느꼈다.
256|
257|왠지 모르게 사혈(死血)을 보고 있다고 생각되는 건 단순한 착각일 거다. 착각이어야 한다.
258|
259|다행히 그의 필사적인 바램이 하늘에 닿았는지, 곧 시선을 거둔 문경이 입을 열었다.
260|
261|“진노하신 적 대협께서 길길이 날뛰셨습니다. 한 번만 더 이런 일이 생긴다면 그때는 정말 각오하라고 하시더군요.”
262|
263|물론 적천강은 길길이 날뛰지도, 저런 말을 하지도 않았다.
264|

Thinking of the Deputy Stronghold Lord traveling comfortably aboard the other swift ship, more than a hundred jang ahead, was enough to make his stomach hurt.

[P56]
*Compared to this, that ship’s a flower garden. A goddamn flower garden.*

[P57]
At least the people aboard the other ship could be reasoned with.

[P58]
Gung Gibang’s smell was a problem you could solve by holding your breath for a moment, and the strange snake Cheongpung called Mimi was surprisingly entertaining to watch when it performed tricks.

[P59]
But this ship?

[P60]
*Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. Fire King Jeok Cheongang. And another old monster hiding his identity.*

[P61]
It was a gathering of monsters.

[P62]
At least Jin Taekyung, his junior in name only, still spoke politely to him. And after seeing Mu Song so often, Jeok Cheongang treated him more or less like a person.

[P63]
The last one was the problem.

[P64]
*Those eyes…*

[P65]
Mu Song shuddered involuntarily at the memory of Mungyeong’s cold gaze.

[P66]
One of the senior river bandits, who had been watching his Stronghold Lord’s strange behavior for some time, came over and asked cautiously, “Stronghold Lord, are you all right?”

[P67]
“Do I look all right?”

[P68]
“Not at all, sir.”

[P69]
“Then why ask? You know what’s going on.”

[P70]
“I worry about you, and that’s the thanks I get? Anyway, what did that old monster threaten you with to make you look so—mmph!”

[P71]
Mu Song’s hand shot out at the speed of light and clamped over his subordinate’s mouth. His eyes darted around the deck.

[P72]
Only after checking twice, then a third time, that no one had heard did his anger surge.

[P73]
“Have you lost your mind? Do you have a death wish?”

[P74]
“Mmph, phew!”

[P75]
The senior river bandit finally pulled free and stammered, “I-I’m sorry, sir. It just slipped out.”

[P76]
“I’ve told you again and again. Neither you nor the others are to say a word about him. Understood?”

[P77]
“Yes, sir.”

[P78]
The senior river bandit was one of the few who had seen Mungyeong’s true identity for himself.

[P79]
Mu Song sighed at the man’s anxious, darting eyes.

[P80]
“More importantly, did you make sure everyone understood the orders I gave earlier?”

[P81]
The senior river bandit nodded.

[P82]
“Yes, sir. Just as you said, I made it clear they’re not to go anywhere near the stern.”

[P83]
“Anyone get suspicious?”

[P84]
There were dozens of river bandits aboard. With that many people, there was bound to be an idiot or two who couldn’t take a hint.

[P85]
“One did. Chunsam. Even after I said it was your order, he asked me about it three times. Nearly gave me a heart attack.”

[P86]
Mu Song ground his teeth.

[P87]
“I knew it’d be that bastard. Where’s Chunsam now?”

[P88]
“We dunked him in the Yangtze and hauled him back out. He’s down below now. He won’t ask again.”

[P89]
“Whew. Good work. Keep the others in line even when I’m away. One slip, and we could all end up at the bottom of the Yangtze, swift ship and all.”

[P90]
Mu Song’s expression darkened.

[P91]
As if the monster known as the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, weren’t enough, now an unidentified old monster who had achieved Returned to Youth was aboard as well. Mu Song almost missed the days when he hadn’t known.

[P92]
Seeing their towering Stronghold Lord in such a state, the senior river bandit asked anxiously, “Are we ever going to make it back to Sichuan? We’ve been away from the stronghold for nearly two months already. I’m worried it’ll stay empty forever.”

[P93]
“Don’t say such unlucky things. They say you can survive even in a tiger’s den if you keep your head.”

[P94]
“That’s a tiger. Against a Returned to Youth Supreme Peak master, I don’t think keeping your head a hundred times over would help…”

[P95]
Come to think of it, he was right.

[P96]
Mu Song had no answer. He shut his mouth.

[P97]
That was when a voice came from behind him.

[P98]
“I brought the liquor barrel. Where should I put it?”

[P99]
There was only one person who would be talking about a liquor barrel right now.

[P100]
Irritation flared. Without even turning around, Mu Song snapped, “I’ve been letting it slide, but that useless bastard has been getting on my nerves since—”

[P101]
“Did you just call me a useless bastard?”

[P102]
“……Huh?”

[P103]
A moment passed that felt like an eternity.

[P104]
The senior river bandit was staring over Mu Song’s shoulder, mouth hanging open. Mu Song knew at once that he was thoroughly fucked.

[P105]
Something else he’d forgotten flashed through his mind.

[P106]
*Ah. The spare liquor barrels are at the stern.*

[P107]
No wonder his subordinate had started to say something when Mu Song told him to bring another one, then stopped.

[P108]
Mu Song felt faint. He hadn’t been afraid even when he was caught in the whirlpool at Tianling Falls, but now he was sweating enough to bathe his neck in it.

[P109]
“Great Hero Mu Song.”

[P110]
Mu Song squeezed his eyes shut. Then he slowly turned around, forcing a smile.

[P111]
The one person he never wanted to meet, even in his dreams, was standing there.

[P112]
“O-oh, Mungyeong. W-what brings you here?”

[P113]
“Nothing in particular.”

[P114]
Mungyeong smiled like any other boy his age.

[P115]
“I was watching the Yangtze from the stern when your subordinate came by. He said Great Hero Mu Song had ordered him to bring a liquor barrel…”

[P116]
“I-I did?”

[P117]
“Didn’t you?”

[P118]
“Well, I… I don’t remember giving an order like that…”

[P119]
A river bandit appeared behind Mungyeong with a barrel on his shoulder and called out briskly, “Stronghold Lord! I brought the liquor barrel you ordered!”

[P120]
Mu Song fought down the urge to tear the man’s mouth apart.

[P121]
“I… I do remember giving that order. Yes. I did. It was a clear mistake.”

[P122]
“A mistake. I see.”

[P123]
Mu Song felt Mungyeong’s gaze travel from one part of his body to another.

[P124]
Surely it was only his imagination that Mungyeong was looking at his lethal acupoints. It had to be.

[P125]
Fortunately, perhaps his desperate wish reached the heavens. Mungyeong withdrew his gaze and spoke.

[P126]
“Great Hero Jeok was beside himself with rage. He said that if it happened again, you’d better be prepared.”

[P127]
Of course, Jeok Cheongang hadn’t flown into a rage or said anything of the sort.

[P128]
But Mu Song wasn’t stupid enough to miss what Mungyeong meant.

[P129]
“Y-yes, I understand. Tell Great Hero Jeok I’ll bear it in mind. But…”

[P130]
“Go ahead.”

[P131]
“What if someone absolutely has to go to the stern? For ship’s business, say. Or to bring meals.”

[P132]
Mungyeong thought for a moment before answering. “Great Hero Jeok told me to pass along instructions for that, too. If it’s ship’s business, you’re to come alone and take care of it. And you’re to deliver the meals yourself.”

[P133]
“……You mean I have to do all that alone?”

[P134]
“Would you rather not?”

[P135]
Mu Song’s face went rigid.

[P136]
“It’s been my lifelong wish. I couldn’t be happier.”

[P137]
“I see. Then I’ll be going. See you at dinner.”

[P138]
Mungyeong headed back toward the stern, leaving Mu Song behind. Then he stopped and turned around.

[P139]
“Oh, and one more thing.”

[P140]
“W-what else?”

[P141]
“Two portions will be enough for each meal until we reach Henan.”

[P142]
“Huh?”

[P143]
“Young Master Jin won’t have much of an appetite for a while. Keep that in mind.”

[P144]
They had at least ten days left before they reached Henan. No matter how poor someone’s appetite was, going ten whole days without eating was absurd.

[P145]
Curiosity got the better of Mu Song. He mustered his courage and asked, “Um… did something happen to Junior Jin?”

[P146]
“Oh.”

[P147]
A dimple appeared beside Mungyeong’s mouth.

[P148]
His smile was so natural that even Mu Song, who thought of him as a monster, mistook him for an innocent boy for an instant.

[P149]
“He should be busy right now. Very busy.”

[P150]
* * *

[P151]
Sometimes I feel like I’ve become a human smartphone.

[P152]
A System window had appeared before my eyes, much like the warning you get when your battery falls below fifteen percent.

[P153]
Beep.

[P154]
> **System**
>
> - Most of your **internal energy** has been depleted.
> - **Circulate your qi** to replenish your internal energy. If it runs out completely, you may suffer a Status abnormality!

[P155]
But why was I more puzzled than alarmed?

[P156]
If I ran out of internal energy right now, I’d sink in the middle of this vast stretch of the Yangtze. Yet the danger bothered me less than the questions.

[P157]
And at least one of those questions had to do with whatever was approaching from far away.

[P158]
Ssssh.

[P159]
A large body drew closer with remarkable stealth. The fin poking above the water looked oddly familiar.

[P160]
*No, fuck.*

[P161]
Why the hell was there a shark in the Yangtze?

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.
